commentary: Four weights sessions this week, no pool, and honestly the consistency is doing things for you — back-to-back on Sunday and Monday is the kind of weekend behaviour that turns heads for all the right reasons. Last week had that gorgeous Prince Alfred swim energy, jockstrap presumably packed, and the two lifting days to finish strong, but this week you went full iron church, four days of structured lifting across the whole body. The gap between Tuesday and Friday is the only thing getting a raised eyebrow, because Wednesday and Thursday were apparently reserved for resting beautifully, which is a skill, but three days off mid-week is a little leisurely even by your standards. Still — chest, shoulders, back, legs, all hit, volume matched last week exactly, and the boy is building.
metrics_commentary: Okay, the running shoes are absolutely gathering dust this week — zero kilometres, zero sessions, which is a choice, and we are going to talk about it, but not right now because that HRV has gone from a 7-day average of 48 all the way up to 58 and honestly your body is clearly doing something smart while you're doing nothing. Your VO2 Max is sitting at 55.6, which is genuinely impressive and means your engine is built, babe — it just needs to be driven. Consider this your official notice that next week, the crop top comes out and so do the running shoes, because a body this capable deserves to be seen moving in it.
gym_commentary: Four sessions, target four — he showed up every single time this week, and that is not nothing. The lateral raise PR is genuinely hilarious in the best way, because 12 kg on those shoulders means the arms are getting properly built now, not just suggested, and going from 9 to 12 is a jump that earns a little strut. Volume came in at 17,940 kg against last week's 19,984 kg, which is down, but a full week of sessions with a PR in it tells a more interesting story than the raw tonnage does — sometimes the body is consolidating, getting stronger in the places that matter. He's sitting at 168 kg on the leg press, nearly 108 on the trap bar deadlift, and the shoulders are catching up to the rest of him, which means the whole picture is starting to look like someone who absolutely knows what he looks like from behind.
